title: Understanding Marcelo Montoya Salary: How to Convert Hourly to Annual Pay in Australia
description: Learn how to convert hourly rates to annual salary using the 38-hour week formula. Includes tax, super, and the National Minimum Wage for 2026–27.
salarySummary: To estimate annual pay, multiply your hourly rate by hours per week (usually 38) and then by 52 weeks; for example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44/hour gives $52,254.80 per year before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the correct formula to convert an hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply that by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax, Medicare levy, and superannuation.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my annual pay calculation?
faqs.a: Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. If you are a casual, you should calculate your annual pay using the loaded rate (base rate × 1.25). For example, the casual National Minimum Wage is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). Always apply the loading before multiplying by hours and weeks.

faqs.q: How is tax and the Medicare levy applied to my annual salary?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, resident tax rates are: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on income between $18,201 and $45,000, 30% on $45,001–$135,000, 37% on $135,001–$190,000, and 45% above $190,000. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. These are deducted from your gross annual pay to give an estimate of take-home pay.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

Whether you're checking a job offer or comparing rates, converting an hourly wage to an annual salary is straightforward. The standard formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For most full-time employees, the typical week is 38 ordinary hours. This is the figure used by the Fair Work Commission for the National Minimum Wage. If you work a different number of hours each week, use your average weekly hours. The result is your gross annual income before tax, Medicare, and super.

### Why 38 hours?

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, which equates to $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the baseline for award/agreement‑free adult employees. If you are covered by an award, your minimum rate may be higher. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for each award, updated from 1 July 2026 with a 4.75% increase.

### Including the fortnight

Some people find it easier to think in fortnights. Your fortnightly gross pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. For example, at the National Minimum Wage, the fortnightly amount is $2,009.80. This can be useful when budgeting or comparing salary packages that are quoted fortnightly.

## Distinguishing Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

Not every employee is paid the National Minimum Wage. Here are the key distinctions:

- **National Minimum Wage**: $26.44 per hour (38‑hour week). Applies to employees not covered by an award or agreement.
- **Award rates**: Minimum wages in modern awards are generally higher. From 1 July 2026, award minimum wages increased by 4.75%. Check the relevant [pay guides](/blog) for your industry.
- **Casual loading**: Casual employees receive an extra 25% on top of the base rate. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour. If you are casual, always calculate your annual pay using the loaded rate. Never enter a rate that already includes loading into a calculator that adds loading again.

### Example: Marcelo Montoya salary

While we don't have specific figures for Marcelo Montoya's salary, the same conversion method applies. If Marcelo were a full‑time employee on an award rate of, say, $30 per hour, his annual gross pay would be $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. If he were casual, the loaded rate would be $37.50 per hour, giving $37.50 × 38 × 52 = $74,100. The formula is universal.

## Tax and the Medicare Levy

Once you have your gross annual figure, you can estimate your take‑home pay using the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the Medicare levy.

**Tax rates 2026–27:**
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% on excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,370 plus 45% on excess over $190,000

**Medicare levy:** Generally 2% of taxable income. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds are not yet confirmed.

For a more detailed breakdown, see our [take‑home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

## Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Employers must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of 12% of your ordinary earnings. This is paid on top of your salary, not deducted from it. The maximum contribution base for 2026–27 is $270,830. Super does not reduce your taxable income for PAYG purposes, but it is an important part of your total remuneration package.

For example, on a gross annual salary of $60,000, the employer would contribute an additional $7,200 to your super fund (12% of $60,000), provided the earnings are below the cap.

## Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and, if applicable, check the casual loading box to add 25% automatically. The calculator then shows your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, plus estimated tax and super. It assumes a 38‑hour week unless you change the hours.

For award‑specific rates, refer to our [reference tables](/data) or the [job pay](/topics/job-pay) topic.

## Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more on super and packaging, visit [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).
